# Verifier calibration crosstab (55-map image generalisation)

**Observation anchor**: Obs 269 (`docs/notes/reflections/working-notes.md`). Direct input to meta-findings Theme T3 (verifier miscalibration).

**Companion auto-generated file**: `calibration_autogen.md` in this directory holds the analysis script's raw output and is regenerated by `scripts/crosstab_verifier_vs_human.py`. This `calibration.md` is the paper-citation source; re-running the script does NOT overwrite it (script hardened 2026-04-24 Session 76; see §10 Reproducibility).

## 1. Executive summary

The Vision Language Model (VLM) verifier on the 55-map image-generalisation run is **miscalibrated in the over-confident direction** across the entire probability range > 0.5 and **discriminates only weakly** between human-confirmed mounds and human-confirmed non-mounds on the VLM-only candidate set. Concretely:

- **Expected Calibration Error (ECE) = 0.2689**; the verifier systematically over-promises in every bin above p = 0.30.
- **AUC = 0.6545** [0.6217, 0.6867] (95 % bootstrap CI, 10,000 resamples, seed 42) — only modestly above the 0.5 no-information baseline.
- **Brier score = 0.3226** [0.2974, 0.3476].
- The gap between predicted and empirical P(mound) is steepest in the highest bin: predicted mean 1.000 but empirical P(mound) = 0.549 (gap −0.451; n = 370 candidates at p > 0.99). Roughly **half the verifier's saturated-high-confidence outputs are wrong**.
- In the low-p tail (p ≤ 0.25, n = 230), **P(mound | p ≤ 0.25) = 0.1739** [0.1265, 0.2241] — non-zero but low, consistent with a residual under-confidence effect for faint / low-contrast real mounds (≥ 40 mound candidates with p ≤ 0.25 exist in the set).

**One-line paper claim**: "The VLM verifier used in the pipeline is substantially over-confident at the high end of its probability range (saturated p = 1.0 predictions are correct only 55 % of the time) and shows only weak discrimination overall (AUC = 0.655), so the verifier cannot discharge the pipeline's confidence calibration unaided."

## 2. Data and inputs

- **Candidate set**: 1,028 VLM-only candidates from the 55-map image-generalisation run, restricted to candidates that survived the initial calibrated human-review pass (see `results/55maps-image-generalisation/human-review.csv`).
- **Ground truth**: human-review labels against a 50 m spatial-tolerance buffer (calibrated UI). 472 human-confirmed mounds (prevalence 0.459 in the VLM-only slice), 556 human-confirmed non-mounds.
- **Verifier probabilities**: the per-candidate `verifier_probability` field, a quantised distribution dominated by a high-end spike at 1.000 (370 rows) and 0.95 (180), a middle cluster at 0.83 (147 rows in (0.70, 0.90]), and a low-end mass of 243 rows in [0.15, 0.30]. Only 13 distinct probability values appear across 1,028 candidates, with the (0.95, 0.99] bin empty — a property that limits any threshold-triage strategy (see Obs 269 "Heavy quantisation").
- **All candidates evaluated at buffer = 50 m**.

## 3. Probability-binned calibration table

| Bin | Count | n_mound | n_not_mound | Mean predicted P | Empirical P(mound) | Gap |
|-----|-------|---------|-------------|------------------|--------------------|-----|
| [0.15, 0.30] | 243 | 44 | 199 | 0.192 | 0.181 | -0.010 |
| (0.30, 0.50] | 75 | 25 | 50 | 0.399 | 0.333 | -0.065 |
| (0.50, 0.70] | 13 | 5 | 8 | 0.692 | 0.385 | -0.308 |
| (0.70, 0.90] | 147 | 84 | 63 | 0.830 | 0.571 | -0.259 |
| (0.90, 0.95] | 180 | 111 | 69 | 0.950 | 0.617 | -0.333 |
| (0.99, 1.00] | 370 | 203 | 167 | 1.000 | 0.549 | -0.451 |

**Expected Calibration Error (ECE):** 0.2689.

Positive gap (empirical > predicted) indicates the verifier is **under-confident** in that bin; negative gap indicates over-confidence. Only the lowest bin is close to calibrated (gap −0.010); every bin above 0.30 is increasingly over-confident, with the severity peaking in the saturated-1.0 bin.

## 4. Reliability diagram

See `reliability-diagram.png`. Points above the y = x line are under-confident bins; points below are over-confident. The plot shows a pronounced downward-slope below the diagonal from 0.5 upward, consistent with the table in §3.

## 5. ROC curve and AUC

- **AUC = 0.6545** (95 % bootstrap CI: 0.6217, 0.6867).

See `roc-curve.png`. The AUC value indicates the verifier discriminates mounds from non-mounds on the VLM-only slice only slightly better than chance. Because the AUC metric is prevalence-invariant, the modest value reflects the verifier's inability to consistently rank a mound above a non-mound even on this high-prevalence slice (0.459).

## 6. Precision-Recall curve

See `pr-curve.png`. The slope of the PR curve mirrors the threshold-sweep pattern in §7 below: precision plateaus around 0.57 in the mid-range (0.50 ≤ threshold ≤ 0.90), consistent with the verifier's inability to push precision higher without sacrificing substantial recall.

## 7. Threshold-sweep table (VLM-only set)

Precision and recall are measured within this slice only; they are **not comparable to full-corpus F1**. `precision_delta_vs_0_15` shows the absolute change from the current 0.15 threshold.

| Threshold | n_accepted | TP (mound) | FP (not_mound) | Precision | Precision delta vs 0.15 | Recall (within set) | F1 (within set) |
|-----------|------------|------------|----------------|-----------|-------------------------|---------------------|-----------------|
| 0.15 | 1028 | 472 | 556 | 0.459 | +0.000 | 1.000 | 0.629 |
| 0.20 | 961 | 465 | 496 | 0.484 | +0.025 | 0.985 | 0.649 |
| 0.30 | 798 | 432 | 366 | 0.541 | +0.082 | 0.915 | 0.680 |
| 0.50 | 711 | 403 | 308 | 0.567 | +0.108 | 0.854 | 0.681 |
| 0.70 | 708 | 403 | 305 | 0.569 | +0.110 | 0.854 | 0.683 |
| 0.90 | 553 | 316 | 237 | 0.571 | +0.112 | 0.669 | 0.617 |
| 0.95 | 550 | 314 | 236 | 0.571 | +0.112 | 0.665 | 0.614 |

Thresholds 0.50, 0.70 are essentially equivalent (`n_accepted` differs by only 3, reflecting the quantisation: few verifier outputs fall between these values). Precision caps at 0.571 and recall falls from 1.000 to 0.665 — the verifier cannot achieve > 57 % precision on the VLM-only slice at any threshold.

## 8. Brier score

- **Overall Brier score:** 0.3226 (95 % bootstrap CI: 0.2974, 0.3476).

### Per-symbol-type Brier score

| Symbol type | n | n_mound | Mean predicted P | Empirical P(mound) | Brier |
|-------------|---|---------|------------------|--------------------|-------|
| bench_mark_on_mound | 92 | 92 | 0.841 | 1.000 | 0.0838 |
| burial_mound | 338 | 338 | 0.848 | 1.000 | 0.0876 |
| not_mound | 556 | 0 | 0.625 | 0.000 | 0.5239 |
| settlement_mound | 13 | 13 | 0.869 | 1.000 | 0.0573 |
| trig_point_on_mound | 29 | 29 | 0.876 | 1.000 | 0.0784 |

Per-symbol Brier scores are strongly driven by class prevalence. The `not_mound` class carries the overall Brier score (0.5239) because the verifier assigns mean predicted P = 0.625 to true non-mounds — this is the direct expression of the over-confidence seen in §3. All mound sub-types have modest Brier scores (0.06 − 0.09) precisely because the verifier *does* push them high; the calibration failure is not an inability to see mounds, it is an inability to *refuse* non-mounds.

## 9. Bootstrap confidence intervals (10,000 resamples, seed 42)

| Statistic | Point | 95% CI lo | 95% CI hi |
|-----------|-------|-----------|-----------|
| AUC | 0.6545 | 0.6217 | 0.6867 |
| Brier | 0.3226 | 0.2974 | 0.3476 |
| P(mound \| p ≤ 0.25) | 0.1739 | 0.1265 | 0.2241 |

## 10. Low-p deep dive (p ≤ 0.25)

- Candidates in tail: **230**.
- Mounds in tail: **40**.
- P(mound | p ≤ 0.25) = **0.1739** (bootstrap 95 % CI: 0.1265, 0.2241).

### Symbol-type breakdown of mounds in the tail

| Symbol type | Count |
|-------------|-------|
| burial_mound | 30 |
| bench_mark_on_mound | 7 |
| trig_point_on_mound | 2 |
| settlement_mound | 1 |

### Top 5 maps by mound count in the tail

| Map | Mounds in tail |
|-----|----------------|
| K-35-077-2 | 5 |
| K-35-053-2 | 3 |
| K-35-067-4 | 3 |
| K-35-076-2 | 3 |
| K-35-062-4_Asenovgrad_4326 | 2 |

A non-zero tail P(mound) of 0.1739 [0.1265, 0.2241] is small but meaningfully above zero — the verifier is missing ~17 % of real mounds in what it flags as very-low-confidence. This is a modest but real under-confidence bias on top of the dominant over-confidence bias at the high end.

## 11. Interpretation guide

- **Under-confidence hypothesis in the tail — FALSIFIED at scale**. The initial hypothesis from a live-review spot-check of 4 / 4 low-p mounds was that the verifier was systematically underweighting faint / low-contrast real mounds. The full analysis rejects this: P(mound | p ≤ 0.25) = 0.1739 is **below** the overall VLM-only prevalence of 0.459 (Obs 269 "Finding 3"). The verifier discriminates correctly at the low end; its failure is at the high end. The tail is still non-zero (40 real mounds below p ≤ 0.25), so p ≤ 0.25 should not be used as a hard drop filter, but the tail's composition is consistent with correct low-confidence rejection of mostly-non-mound cases, not with systematic under-confidence.
- **Over-confidence at the high end**: the dominant calibration defect. Saturated-high-confidence outputs (p = 1.000) are correct only 54.9 % of the time. This is the direct driver of the ECE = 0.269 headline.
- **Threshold choice**: precision rises monotonically with threshold; recall (within-set) falls. For archaeological fieldwork-seeding, recall is preferred at the cost of manual review, so a low accept-threshold (~0.15) is still preferable despite modest precision. For a publication-grade detector asking "how confident should I be in a flagged mound?", the answer is: not very — even p = 1.0 predictions are a coin flip with weighting.
- **Per-class Brier**: `not_mound` carries the overall Brier (0.5239). The verifier handles the mound sub-classes well in isolation (each sub-class Brier < 0.09) but fails to reject non-mounds; the failure is *rejection-specific*.

## 12. Caveats / risk register

1. **VLM-only slice is prevalence-skewed**. Mound prevalence on the VLM-only slice is 0.459 — substantially higher than the full-corpus detection prevalence. Calibration metrics generalise to the VLM-proposer's output distribution, not to the broader corpus. A full-corpus calibration analysis would require scoring the verifier on a representative corpus sample including tiles with zero VLM candidates, which is out of scope for this artefact.
2. **Quantisation of verifier output**. The verifier's probability outputs are heavily discrete (5 dominant modes). ECE is computed with bin boundaries at [0.15, 0.30, 0.50, 0.70, 0.90, 0.95, 1.00] to reflect the actual distribution; moving bin edges would change the ECE value by 0.01–0.03. The headline ECE figure is robust to sensible re-binning but is not a single-number summary independent of binning choice.
3. **Single human reviewer**. The human-review labels are from a single reviewer using the calibrated UI. Inter-reviewer calibration bias is out of scope; see `uncalibrated-vs-calibrated-crosstab/crosstab.md` for the within-reviewer UI-effect quantification (21.4 % flip rate).
4. **No per-symbol calibration curve is published here**. The §8 per-symbol Brier table captures the central finding (the rejection-specific failure); a per-symbol reliability diagram would be a useful polish but is not required for paper-citation.
5. **P(mound | p ≤ 0.25) estimate is coarse**. Tail sample n = 230, with 40 mounds; the bootstrap CI width of ~0.10 reflects the limited positive-class count. A sharper estimate would require a larger low-p sample from a separate review round.

## 13. Paper implications

### 13.1 Verifier alone cannot discharge confidence

The combination of modest discrimination (AUC = 0.655) and substantial over-confidence (ECE = 0.269) at the high end means the verifier's probability output is not a reliable per-candidate confidence estimate. A paper-grade detector cannot use `verifier_probability` as the sole confidence signal; pipelines relying on a verifier filter must combine it with additional signal (e.g., candidate provenance, consensus vote share, spatial-attractor heuristics).

### 13.2 Architectural complement with attractor-pull scale

The saturated-high-confidence output bin is exactly the range that the buffer-band lift analysis (`buffer-band-lift/report.md`, Obs 272) identifies as including detections pulled from 50–125 m away from their mounds. The verifier cannot filter these because it already rates them at p = 1.0. This is the Theme T5 architectural finding: no post-hoc verifier filter can relax the 125 m tolerance cap without new information.

### 13.3 Threshold recommendation

For downstream fieldwork seeding: **retain the 0.15 accept threshold** (as used in the production pipeline). Precision rises only modestly with a higher threshold (plateau at 0.571 by threshold = 0.50) while recall drops substantially (to 0.854 at t = 0.50, to 0.669 at t = 0.90). The higher-threshold operating points trade recall for small precision gains; the archaeological use-case favours recall.

### 13.4 Suggested paper text (Results — verifier calibration)

> A calibration analysis of the VLM verifier's probability output against human-review labels on the 55-map image-generalisation VLM-only candidate set (n = 1,028; 472 mounds, 556 non-mounds) finds substantial over-confidence and only modest discrimination. ECE = 0.269; AUC = 0.655 [0.622, 0.687] (95 % bootstrap CI, 10,000 resamples, seed 42); Brier = 0.323 [0.297, 0.348]. Probability-bin gaps range from -0.010 (lowest bin, roughly calibrated) to -0.451 (saturated high-confidence bin; p = 1.000 predictions are correct 54.9 % of the time). The per-symbol Brier breakdown shows the calibration failure is rejection-specific: each mound sub-type is assigned appropriately high mean predicted probabilities (0.841 – 0.876, Brier 0.057 – 0.088), whereas non-mounds receive mean predicted probability 0.625 (Brier 0.524). The verifier cannot, on its own, discharge the pipeline's confidence estimate.

- **Guardrail (Session 75 item 6 / Session 76 carry-over)**: the script was hardened on 2026-04-24 to redirect its Markdown output from `calibration.md` to `calibration_autogen.md`, protecting this hand-authored level-up against dry-run overwrite.

    ```bash
    python scripts/crosstab_verifier_vs_human.py \
        --review results/55maps-image-generalisation/human-review.csv \
        --detections outputs/55maps-image-generalisation/verified/verified_detections.geojson \
    ```
